subject: Banking
title: The $81 Million Bangladesh Heist
description: A fast breakdown of The $81 Million Bangladesh Heist for builders.

hook.text: In 2016, hackers stole $81 million from Bangladesh's central bank by sending fake SWIFT messages to the New York Fed.

buildup.text: The attackers gained access to Bangladesh Bank's SWIFT terminal and sent 35 fraudulent transfer requests totaling $951.

discovery.text: A spelling error in one request raised a flag. The word 'fandation' instead of 'foundation' stopped most transfers.

twist.text: Five transfers totaling $81 million went through before anyone noticed.

climax.text: A typo saved $870 million. The heist exposed that even the world's most secure payment network has human weak points.

punchline.text: A typo stopped $870M in theft. $81M still vanished through SWIFT.

quiz.question: What accidentally prevented the full $951 million theft?
options: A spelling error in a transfer request raised suspicion

details.summary: In 2016, hackers breached Bangladesh Bank's systems and used fraudulent SWIFT messages to steal 81 million dollars from the bank's account at the New York Federal Reserve, exposing critical vulnerabilities in global payment infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: The Bangladesh Bank heist revealed that even the most trusted financial messaging system could be exploited through weak endpoint security, prompting a global overhaul of SWIFT security standards.
takeaways: Hackers sent 35 fraudulent SWIFT transfer requests totaling nearly 1 billion dollars
A spelling error in one request triggered suspicion and blocked most transfers
The attack originated from malware installed on Bangladesh Bank's SWIFT terminal

faq.question: How did the hackers get access to the SWIFT system?
faq.answer: Malware was installed on Bangladesh Bank's computers through social engineering. The bank's SWIFT terminal had poor security, including no firewall and second-hand network switches. The hackers spent months studying the system before striking.

faq.question: Was the stolen money ever recovered?
faq.answer: Only about 15 million of the 81 million was recovered. Most was laundered through Philippine casinos. The attack was attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group, and recovery from a state-sponsored actor proved nearly impossible.
